A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SiMEC/SiMExp research, and their supplied text, equations and graphics are readable. v1 includes a supplementary appendix; v2 references supplementary material that is neither appended nor embedded, limiting comparison of proofs and full experimental details.

before.justification: v1 reports original MNIST and BERT experiments, runtime and perturbation comparisons, and quantitative HateXplain feature-importance results. Its appendix includes additional experimental findings.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on MNIST, CIFAR10, WinoBias and Measuring-Hate-Speech, including probability trajectories, ranking changes, exploration volumes and decoding consistency.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 replace v1's steps of 1/sqrt(lambda_max) and 2/sqrt(lambda_max) with the same condition-number-based rule, eta*sqrt(min_nonzero|lambda|/max|lambda|), for both algorithms. The null/non-null eigendirection framework remains, but v1's standalone eigenvalue-based feature-importance algorithm is also omitted from v2's presented method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates MNIST, ChatGPT-generated classification and masked-language sentences, and HateXplain attribution annotations. v2 retains MNIST and introduces CIFAR10 object images, WinoBias gender-bias-focused language data, and Measuring-Hate-Speech. Its reported evaluation no longer includes the annotated feature-importance task.

E2.justification: v1 compares exploration against label-dependent, semi-random image perturbations and attribution against Attention Rollout and Chefer et al.'s Relevancy. v2 instead evaluates gradient-based Gaussian-noise embedding baselines with separate directions for preserving or changing classes. The attribution comparators are absent from its reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Although 1000 exploration iterations remain, v2 introduces eta=1/10 experiments and matches its baselines by iteration count and average step, replacing v1's equal-time comparison. New protocols measure embedding probabilities, ranking inversions, PCA-based exploration volume, output diversity and Wasserstein consistency, substantially revising the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 adds step-size sensitivity tests, exploration-volume analysis, and quantitative investigation of disagreement and subsequent realignment between embedding and decoded predictions. Its CIFAR10/MHS trajectory case studies also examine exploration direction. These extend substantially beyond v1's image-quality comparison, attribution examples and supplementary MLM failure observation.

E5.justification: v1 already reports means and standard deviations. v2 additionally describes aggregation over multiple runs and inputs, identifies plotted standard deviations, and introduces Welch t-tests for exploration volumes and Pearson-correlation p-values. Exact run counts and seeds remain unspecified; an increase in repeated runs cannot be established.

E6.justification: v1's HateXplain similarities—0.707 for the proposed method, 0.700 for Relevancy and 0.583 for Attention Rollout—are no longer reported. v2 adds ranking-change results, including CIFAR10 SiMExp means of 2.60 at eta=1 and 18.70 at eta=10, and decoding-distance medians of 0.0/0.049 for SiMEC/SiMExp. These are new measurements under revised settings, not established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The main propositions largely remain. Visible changes include correcting Corollary 1's relation from N_(i+1) to N_i and adding an explicit embedding-domain bound. However, v1 supplies additional assumptions and proofs in its appendix, while v2's supplementary material is unavailable, preventing a reliable assessment of the full extent of theoretical revision.

C1.justification: v1 presents feature-importance explanations as an achieved application alongside input exploration. v2's abstract and conclusion focus on preserving or changing output distributions and interpreting alternative inputs, while feature-based explainability becomes a future objective. This substantially narrows the contribution scope while retaining the central exploration claim.

C2.justification: v1 already cautions that decoding does not preserve every embedding update. v2 develops an explanation involving loose feasible-region bounds and decoder errors, interprets larger explored volumes as directional exploration, and discusses delayed prediction alignment. It also identifies scalability to larger embedding dimensions as an unresolved objective.

D1.justification: v2 adds a specific code-repository URL and explicit information about embedding bounds and invertible ViT embeddings. Its reported hardware changes from A100/Ubuntu 20.04 to H100/Ubuntu 22.04. Unlike v1's concrete ViT architecture and training recipe, fuller model and experimental details are deferred to the unavailable supplement.

R1.justification: The feature-attribution literature discussion is removed. v2 adds substantial positioning against geometric foliations and Fisher-information approaches, including Grementieri and Fioresi and work by Tron and coauthors, plus additional Benfenati–Marta papers. It distinguishes its Transformer setting, interpretation procedure and adaptive exploration steps from these predecessors.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around the two exploration objectives. Section 3.2 changes from feature importance plus interpretation to interpretation alone; the experimental narrative is reordered and rewritten, as are related work and conclusions. This exceeds local language editing despite retaining the main section skeleton.

P2.justification: v1's attribution heatmaps, MNIST reconstruction panel and separate decoded-output plots give way to v2's combined CIFAR10/MHS trajectory figure, multi-dataset probability and baseline plots, and new ranking-change Table 1. Algorithm boxes are consolidated and repositioned, and the title-page author layout is compressed.

improvement.justification: v2 provides more focused validation through broader data coverage, step-size tests and quantitative decoding-consistency analysis, addressing weaknesses in v1's preliminary evidence. However, v1's included proofs are absent from the supplied v2, and important experimental details are deferred to unavailable supplementary material. These gains and losses in verifiability prevent a confident overall-quality judgment.
